A driver cannot know this — it holds credentials, not the row they
were unsealed from — so it is stamped by the control plane as it
merges each account's catalog. Without it a caller could not turn a
choice from the merged list back into a request, which names the

whatever hardware it has, and flyco does not learn that until a
daemon runs on it and says so — inventing a size here would be a
number the agent could plan against and be wrong about.

Carried rather than worked out by the client: the first row of the
first page *is* the default branch, and a client deriving that for
itself would be repeating the question the control plane already
asked GitHub.

name.description: The branch, as git spells it.

BudgetStage.description: How far through the budget the session is. Monotonically increasing.

BudgetView.description:
Budget accounting as the API serves it.

Every field is derived from replaying the spend ledger through
[`BudgetState`], so the API can never disagree with the engine.

remaining.description: Left to spend; zero once exhausted.

stage.description: How far through the budget the session is.

Callback.description: Query string GitHub appends when it redirects back.

state.description: The `state` this control plane minted in [`start`].

CatalogFilter.description:
Narrows the machine catalog.

Every field is optional: an unfiltered catalog is the honest default,
because a user with one linked provider should not have to name it.

oneOf.description:
Only machines this linked account can deploy.

Narrower than [`Self::provider`], and a different question: a user
with two Azure subscriptions is choosing between two bills, and a
card that spoke for both of them would name a machine the account it
sits on cannot create.
Only machines running this operating system family.
Only machines from this provider.

region.description: Only machines in this provider-native region.

ClaudeOauthStart.description:
Response of `POST /v1/harness-accounts/claude/oauth/start`.

The PKCE verifier never appears here: it stays in the control plane's
key-value store for the ten minutes the attempt lives, and the browser
carries only the opaque attempt id that names it.

attempt_id.description:
Names the verifier and `state` the completion must be redeemed
against.

CloudUsageFilter.description: Narrows the cloud usage panel to one provider.

oneOf.description: Only accounts with this provider.

CloudUsageView.description:
One row of `GET /v1/usage/cloud`, covering one linked account over one
billing period.

account.description: Account the spend is billed to.

period_end_unix.description: End of the billing period, seconds since the Unix epoch.

period_start_unix.description: Start of the billing period, seconds since the Unix epoch.

spent.description: Spend the provider has metered so far this period.

CodexOauthPending.description:
Body of a `GET /v1/harness-accounts/codex/oauth/{attempt_id}` that found
the sign-in still waiting.

An approved sign-in answers `201` with the linked
[`HarnessAccountView`] instead, so the two outcomes are told apart by
the status code and never by a nullable field.

CodexOauthStart.description:
Response of `POST /v1/harness-accounts/codex/oauth/start`.

The three things `codex login --device-auth` prints, plus the opaque
attempt id the browser polls against. `OpenAI`'s `device_auth_id` is
deliberately not among them: it is the half that redeems the grant, so
it stays in the control plane's key-value store beside the user who
started the attempt.

attempt_id.description: Names the device authorization this sign-in is polled against.

interval_seconds.description: How long to wait between polls, as `OpenAI` states it.

user_code.description:
The one-time code the user types at
[`verification_url`](Self::verification_url).

verification_url.description:
Where the user approves the code, which is
`https://auth.openai.com/codex/device`.

attempt_id.description: The attempt this code belongs to, from [`ClaudeOauthStart`].

code.description:
What Anthropic showed the user, which is `CODE#STATE` — the bare
code alone is accepted too, because a user who selects only the
first half of it has still supplied everything the exchange needs.

ContextWindow.description:
How full the model's context window is.

Reported as a pair or not at all: a fill gauge needs both numbers, and a
harness that names only one of them tells us nothing displayable.

size_tokens.description: Size of the context window in tokens.

used_tokens.description: Tokens currently occupying the context window.

CpuArchitecture.description:
The instruction set a machine type runs.

An independent dimension of the catalog rather than a property to rank:
an arm64 type is not a cheaper or dearer version of an x86-64 one, it is
a different machine, and a build that needs one is not served by the
other. Curation therefore never compares across it (see
[`crate::catalog`]).

label.description:
Human-readable name, shown in the key list so a key can be recognised
before it is revoked.

oneOf.description: Parent to hang the node under; omitted creates a root.
Repository the node is about; omitted makes it shared.

title.description: Short title shown when listing children.

branch.description:
Branch to check out. Untyped for the same reason as
[`repo`](Self::repo): the control plane parses it into a
[`BranchName`](crate::repo::BranchName) and refuses anything git
would.

Omitted, the control plane asks GitHub for the repository's default
branch and records *that*, so a session always names the branch it
works on rather than leaving every later reader to guess.

budget_limit.description: Spending limit for the whole session.

harness.description: Which coding harness drives the session.

oneOf.description:
The machine to provision for it.

Omitted, flyco picks the cheapest Linux type in the caller's catalog
of at least
[`AUTO_MIN_VCPUS`](crate::machine::AUTO_MIN_VCPUS) vCPUs and
[`AUTO_MIN_MEMORY_MIB`](crate::machine::AUTO_MIN_MEMORY_MIB) of
memory, and records the machine as automatically chosen.

prompt.description:
What the agent should do first.

Required, because a session with nothing to do is a machine nobody
asked for: the prompt is recorded as the session's first user
message and delivered to the daemon as soon as one connects. Its
excerpt is also the session's opening [`title`](SessionSummary::title).

repo.description:
Repository to work in, `owner/name`. Untyped here because it is
untrusted input; the control plane parses it into a
[`RepoSlug`](crate::repo::RepoSlug) and rejects anything else.

spot.description:
Whether to ask for interruptible spot capacity when flyco picks the
machine. Ignored when [`Self::machine`] names a type, because that
choice already carries its own `spot`.

CreatedApiKey.description:
A freshly minted API key.

This is the only representation that ever carries the plaintext
[`token`](Self::token): the control plane stores nothing but its hash, so
a key that is not saved here is gone.

created_at_unix.description: Creation time, seconds since the Unix epoch.

id.description: Identifier used to revoke the key later.

label.description: Label supplied at creation.

token.description: The plaintext key, returned exactly once.

The authenticated caller behind a request.

Produced by the control plane's authenticator from either credential
shape, and returned verbatim by `GET /v1/me`.

id.description: The flyco user this request acts as.

login.description: The caller's GitHub login, cached at sign-in.

session_cap.description:
How many sessions this user may hold at once, counting everything
that is not archived.

DaemonToken.description:
A freshly minted daemon token.

Response of `POST /v1/sessions/{id}/daemon-token`. Minting again
replaces the previous token, so a session has at most one live daemon
credential and re-pairing revokes the old one.

session.description: The session this token authenticates a daemon for.

token.description: The plaintext token, returned exactly once.

DefaultMachineQuery.description: Whether a caller who names no machine wants interruptible capacity.

oneOf.description:
Answer for this linked account alone.

What a compute card asks: "if this were the only account, what would
flyco run on?" Absent, the answer is drawn from every linked account,
which is what the composer's chip shows.

spot.description:
Whether to price and pick against spot capacity. Spot is the default
because it is cheaper and flyco handles eviction.

entries.description: Every variable the session runs with, in the order it is stored.

warning.description:
[`NETWORK_CONTROL_WARNING`], repeated on every response so a client
renders the caveat beside the values rather than hard-coding it.

EnvEntry.description: One `KEY=value` pair of a session's environment.

key.description: Variable name, as the harness process will see it.

EventCursor.description: Where in a session's event stream to resume reading.

after.description: Return events strictly after this position.

EventPage.description: A page of the room's event tail.

more.description: Whether more events exist past the last one returned.

Feature.description: A harness capability tracked in the per-harness feature matrix.

HarnessAccountView.description:
A Claude or Codex account the user has linked, as `GET
/v1/harness-accounts` lists it.

No representation of an account carries its credential; the sealed value
leaves the control plane only when it is provisioned onto a session machine.

expires_at_unix.description:
When the stored credential expires, when the vendor states a
lifetime.

label.description:
Account name as the vendor reports it, so the user can tell two
linked accounts apart.

linked_at_unix.description: When it was linked, seconds since the Unix epoch.

oneOf.description: Long-lived Claude subscription token produced by `claude setup-token`.
Anthropic API key used by Claude Code.
`OpenAI` API key used by Codex.

A Claude subscription obtained through the OAuth code flow.

The pair the flow yields rather than a single token: the access
token is what a session's machine runs the agent under, and the
refresh token is what keeps a linked account working past the
access token's lifetime without the user pasting anything again.

expires_at_unix.description:
When the access token stops working, seconds since the Unix
epoch.

refresh_token.description: Redeemed for a new pair once the access token is near its end.

oneOf.description:
A `ChatGPT` subscription obtained through the Codex device-code flow.

Four values rather than one, because Codex's own `auth.json` is four
values: the id token names the account, the access token runs the
agent, the refresh token keeps the link alive, and the account id is
the workspace every request is billed to.

access_token.description: The bearer token Codex runs under, until it expires.

account_id.description: `chatgpt_account_id`, the workspace the grant belongs to.

expires_at_unix.description:
When the access token stops working, seconds since the Unix
epoch.

id_token.description: The `ChatGPT` id token, a JWT naming the account.

refresh_token.description: Redeemed for a new set once the access token is near its end.

HarnessCredentialInput.description:
A credential accepted when linking a Claude Code or Codex account.

Each variant determines its harness, so the wire format cannot pair a
Claude credential with Codex or vice versa. Secret fields are deliberately
omitted from [`Debug`](core::fmt::Debug).

HarnessFeature.description: One row of the per-harness feature matrix.

HarnessKind.description:
The coding harness driving a session. Flyco supports exactly these two
and never builds its own.

HarnessObservation.description:
One thing a session's daemon saw happen to the harness account driving
it, as `POST /v1/sessions/{id}/harness-observations` records it.

The daemon is the only place both facts exist: it holds the turn's
[`UsageReport`](crate::harness::UsageReport) and it is what receives
[`HarnessEvent::UsageLimited`](crate::harness::HarnessEvent::UsageLimited).
Neither can be asked for after the fact, which is why they are posted as
they happen rather than polled.

An observation that reports neither is nothing to record, and the
control plane refuses it rather than storing a row that says nothing.

oneOf.description:
Cost the harness reported for the turn that just finished, when it
reported one.
Present when this observation is the account hitting its limit.

HarnessSessionIdentity.description: The harness-native session id the daemon announced at start.

harness_session_id.description: Identity the harness minted; resume reopens this conversation.

HeaderEntry.description: One HTTP header sent with every request to a remote MCP server.

wire_protocol_version.description: Wire protocol version this control plane speaks to daemons.

LinkHarnessAccount.description: Request to link a Claude Code or Codex account.

credential.description: Authentication material, tagged with the mode that consumes it.

label.description: User-facing name that distinguishes this credential from another.

credentials.description: The credentials to seal. Their variant names the provider.

label.description:
Human-readable name, so an account can be recognised in a list before
it is unlinked.

LlmUsageView.description:
One row of `GET /v1/usage/llm`, covering one linked harness account.

Every field is an observation rather than a quota. A panel built from
this says "you have spent this much and were limited at this time",
which is the honest claim; "you have N requests left" is not one flyco
can make.

label.description: Label the account was linked under.

oneOf.description:
Cost the harness itself reported over that window, summed from its
telemetry. Absent when the harness reported none.

period_start_unix.description:
Start of the window these observations cover, seconds since the Unix
epoch.

rate_limited_at_unix.description: When this account last hit its usage limit, if it has.

resets_at_unix.description: When that limit resets, when the harness named a time.

MachineCapacity.description:
How much compute a catalog entry offers.

Absent from an entry the provider does not publish a size for — see
[`MachineCatalogEntry::capacity`].

MachineCatalogEntry.description:
One entry in the machine catalog the agent sees when deciding whether
to keep, upgrade, or downgrade its machine.

oneOf.description:
Which linked account offers it.

A driver cannot know this — it holds credentials, not the row they
were unsealed from — so it is stamped by the control plane as it
merges each account's catalog. Without it a caller could not turn a
choice from the merged list back into a request, which names the
account it provisions through.

How big it is, when the provider publishes a size.

A cloud SKU always does. A host the user registered over SSH has
whatever hardware it has, and flyco does not learn that until a
daemon runs on it and says so — inventing a size here would be a
number the agent could plan against and be wrong about.

Where it sits in the provider's line-up, when the provider says.

Absent for the same reason [`Self::capacity`] is: a host the user
registered is whatever hardware it is, and flyco has not looked.

pricing.description: What it costs to run for an hour.

region.description:
Provider-native region this entry is offered in.

A catalog spans every region an account may deploy into, so an entry
without one would not say where the machine it describes can be
created. A registered SSH host names itself here: it is its own
region, and there is nowhere else to put it.

MachineChoice.description:
Which machine a session asks for.

Named on [`CreateSession`] when the caller picks a type themselves. The
choice is validated against the named account's own catalog before
anything is written, so a machine the account cannot deploy is refused
where the user made the choice. Omitted, flyco picks a machine itself
with [`auto_linux_choice`](crate::machine::auto_linux_choice) instead of
guessing and resizing afterwards, and the session records that the
choice was flyco's ([`MachineOrigin::Auto`]).

machine_type.description: Provider-native machine type, as `GET /v1/machines/catalog` names it.

provider_account.description: Which linked provider account to provision on.

region.description: Provider-native region, as the catalog entry names it.

spot.description:
Whether to ask for interruptible spot capacity. Spot is the default
because it is the cheaper option and flyco handles eviction.

A request, not a promise: a provider that cannot honour it is
answered with on-demand capacity, and
[`MachineView::spot`](crate::machine::MachineView::spot) is what was
actually obtained.

MachineDefault.description:
Answer of `GET /v1/machines/default`.

The machine flyco would provision right now, and the catalog entry it
came from, so a caller can show what it costs and how big it is without
searching the whole catalog for the type flyco named. The two travel
together because they are one answer: a choice whose entry the caller had
to look up again could be looked up against a catalog that has since
changed.

choice.description: What `POST /v1/sessions` would provision if it named no machine.

entry.description: The catalog entry that choice points at, with its price and size.

MachineLineage.description:
Where a machine type sits in its provider's own line-up.

The three facts curation needs, and none of which a frontend should ever
recover by parsing a type name: which instruction set it runs, which
family of the provider's line-up it belongs to, and which generation of
that family it is. Every driver derives them from the metadata its own
API publishes — Azure's quota family, EC2's `DescribeInstanceTypes`,
Compute Engine's `architecture` field and series name — so a provider
that renames its types breaks one driver rather than the whole product.

Absent from an entry describing hardware the user owns: flyco has not
inspected that machine, and inventing a family for it would be a claim
the catalog cannot support.

family.description:
Provider-native family key, with the generation removed.

Two types share a family when the provider sells them as the same
machine in different generations: `Standard_D4s_v5` and
`Standard_D4s_v6`, `m6g.xlarge` and `m7g.xlarge`. The string is a
key rather than a label — its shape is the driver's business, and
nothing outside the driver that produced it may parse it.

generation.description:
Which generation of that family it is, when the provider numbers
them.

Absent where a family carries no version in the provider's own
metadata, which makes it a family of one rather than an old
generation to hide.

MachineOrigin.description:
How the machine a session runs on was chosen.

Persisted because the two are not interchangeable afterwards: a machine
the user picked is a decision flyco must not quietly undo, while an
automatic one is flyco's own guess and is free to be revisited.

oneOf.description: The provider meters this machine and bills for it by the hour.

The floor the provider bills the moment the machine boots, when
it imposes one (e.g. EC2 Mac dedicated hosts bill 24 hours under
the Apple licence). The agent and the user both see this before
choosing.
Spot price per hour, when the type is available as spot.

storage.description: Persistent-disk pricing published by the provider.

oneOf.description:
Hardware the user already owns and already pays for. Flyco meters
nothing on it and a session running here spends no budget.

MachinePricing.description:
What an hour on a machine costs.

A sum rather than an amount with a nullable field, because "the provider
bills nothing for this" and "the price is zero" are different claims and
only one of them is ever true. A machine the user already owns has no
rate flyco could quote, and quoting `$0.00` would tell a budget it can
run forever.

MachineSpec.description: Everything needed to provision a machine for a session.

spot.description: Whether to request spot capacity (the default).

MachineState.description: Lifecycle state of a provisioned machine.

MachineView.description:
The machine a session is running on, as `GET
/v1/sessions/{id}/machine` reports it.

created_at_unix.description: When it was created, seconds since the Unix epoch.

oneOf.description:
Price actually being billed per hour — the spot price when the
machine holds spot capacity, the on-demand one otherwise, and
nothing at all on hardware the user owns.

session.description: Session it belongs to. A machine serves exactly one.

spot.description:
Whether the machine actually holds interruptible capacity.

[`spec.spot`](MachineSpec::spot) is what was asked for; this is what
the provider gave. Azure refuses spot on subscriptions and SKUs that
do not support it, and flyco falls back to on-demand rather than
failing the session, so the two can disagree — and the price being
billed follows this field, not the request.

state.description: Where it is in its lifecycle.

oneOf.description: Persistent-disk price actually being billed per hour.

A process the daemon launches on the session machine and speaks to
over stdio.

env.description: Extra environment for the process, on top of the session's.

oneOf.description: A remote server reached over streamable HTTP.

headers.description: Headers sent with every request, typically an authorization.

McpServerConfig.description:
How a session reaches one MCP server.

The transport is the tag, so a stdio server can never carry a URL and a
remote one can never carry a command line.

name.description: Name the harness announces it under.

updated_at_unix.description: Last change, seconds since the Unix epoch.

MemoryFilter.description: Which level of the tree to list.

oneOf.description: List this node's children. Omitted lists the roots.

repo.description:
Only nodes about this repository, `owner/name`. Omitted lists the
memory that applies wherever the caller's agents run.

MemoryNode.description: One node in the memory tree.

oneOf.description: Parent node; `None` for a root.

Repository this subtree is about; `None` for memory that applies
wherever the user's agents run.

title.description: Short title shown when listing children.

updated_at_unix.description: Last update as a unix timestamp in seconds.

OsFamily.description: Operating system family of a machine type.

Problem.description:
An RFC 9457 problem detail document.

`instance` is deliberately absent: flyco has no per-occurrence URI to
point at yet.

detail.description: Human-readable explanation of this particular occurrence.

status.description: The HTTP status code, repeated in the body as RFC 9457 advises.

title.description: Short, human-readable summary of the problem type.

type.description:
URI identifying the problem type, or [`ABOUT_BLANK`] when the status
code carries all the meaning there is.

id.description: Identifier used to unlink the account.

label.description: Label supplied when it was linked.

linked_at_unix.description: When it was linked, seconds since the Unix epoch.

ProviderBonusHint.description: One suggestion returned by the quickstart questionnaire.

oneOf.description: Headline credit, when the programme states a fixed amount.

detail.description: What the user has to do to claim it.

title.description: Name of the programme, as the provider calls it.

oneOf.description:
An Azure service principal, `Contributor` on a whole subscription.

Subscription scope rather than resource-group scope, because that is
what `az ad sp create-for-rbac --role Contributor --scopes
/subscriptions/…` produces and what lets flyco create the resource
group it owns instead of asking the user to make one and name it.

admin_ssh_public_key.description:
The `OpenSSH` public key a machine's break-glass login is created
with.

Azure refuses to create a Linux machine with neither a password
nor a key and flyco sets no passwords, so one is required. It is
the *user's* key: the wizard generates the pair in their browser,
offers them the private half once, and sends only this. Flyco
never holds a private key for a machine it provisions.

client_id.description: Application (client) id of the service principal.

client_secret.description: Client secret issued for that application.

tenant_id.description: Directory (tenant) the service principal belongs to.

oneOf.description: An AWS IAM access key.

key_name.description:
Name of an EC2 key pair in the user's own account, for a
break-glass login.

Optional, unlike Azure's public key: EC2 creates an instance
perfectly well without one. It is the *user's* key pair either
way — flyco never holds a private key for a machine it
provisions, and a key pair lives in their account, not in
flyco's.

session_token.description:
Session token, for a temporary credential.

Absent for the long-lived IAM key most users will paste in.
Present, and required, for anything minted by `sts:AssumeRole` —
a signature made without it is refused however correct it is.

oneOf.description: A GCP service account key, as the JSON document Google issues.

A Linux host the user already owns, reached over SSH and sandboxed
with Podman.

host_fingerprint.description:
The host key flyco must see, as `ssh-keygen -lf` prints it:
`SHA256:` followed by unpadded base64.

Required rather than optional, and there is no trust-on-first-use
path: linking this account is the moment flyco starts handing the
host live session credentials, and an unverified host key means
handing them to whoever answers on that address.

private_key.description: PEM-encoded private key flyco authenticates with.

user.description: Login user, which must be able to run Podman.

ProviderCredentials.description:
Provider-native credentials, tagged by the provider they open.

The tag *is* the provider: an account's kind is read off the variant
rather than carried beside it, so a request cannot name Azure and enclose
an AWS key pair.

ProvisioningStage.description:
How far a session's machine has got towards running an agent.

Provisioning takes minutes, and a spinner for those minutes tells the
user nothing about whether anything is wrong. The stages are the five
milestones flyco can actually observe, in the order they happen, and the
session page renders them as a timeline inside the transcript
(docs/ux.md §9.2).

Who announces which is decided by who can see it: the control plane's
provisioning queue owns everything up to the machine existing, and the
daemon on that machine owns everything after it boots.

PushKeys.description:
The two keys a browser derives for message encryption ([RFC 8291]).

[RFC 8291]: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8291

auth.description: The client's authentication secret, base64url without padding.

p256dh.description: The client's P-256 public key, base64url without padding.

PushSubscription.description:
Request body of `POST /v1/push/subscriptions`: a browser
`PushSubscription`, serialized by the browser.

endpoint.description: The push service endpoint this browser's messages are posted to.

expirationTime.description:
When the subscription expires, in milliseconds since the Unix epoch,
on the rare push service that sets one. Milliseconds rather than
seconds because that is what the browser reports.

PushSubscriptionView.description:
Response of `POST /v1/push/subscriptions`.

Carries the endpoint back but never the keys: they are write-only, and a
subscription is identified from here on by [`id`](Self::id).

created_at_unix.description: When it was registered, seconds since the Unix epoch.

endpoint.description: The push service endpoint it posts to.

id.description: Identifier used to remove the subscription.

QuickstartAnswers.description:
Request body of `POST /v1/providers/quickstart`.

Two questions, because two questions are what separate the free-credit
programmes worth telling somebody about from the ones that would waste
their time.

is_student.description: Whether the user is a student, which unlocks the education tiers.

new_to_provider.description:
Whether the user has never held an account with these providers, and
so still qualifies for new-customer credit.

RateLimitObservation.description:
The account hit its usage limit.

A struct rather than a bare timestamp field beside the cost, so "when it
resets" cannot be set on an observation that is not a rate limit: the
reset time only exists inside the event that has one.

resets_at_unix.description: When the harness said the limit resets, when it named a time.

expires_at_unix.description: When it stops being accepted, seconds since the Unix epoch.

ticket.description:
The single-use ticket, to be passed as the `ticket` query parameter
of the client relay route.

q.description:
Substring to match against `owner/name`. Omitted lists the caller's
repositories by most recent push.

RepoStatus.description:
The working tree of a session's checkout, as `GET
/v1/sessions/{id}/repo-status` reports it.

Dirtiness is load-bearing rather than informational: an agent may not
stop while the tree is dirty, and archiving a dirty session warns the
user before the disk is released. The UI needs the same fact.

dirty.description: Whether the working tree has changes that are not committed.

summary.description: `git status --short`, as the daemon last read it. Empty when clean.

default_branch.description: Branch a session starts from unless the user names another.

description.description: GitHub's description, when the repository has one.

pushed_at_unix.description:
Last push, seconds since the Unix epoch, so the picker can order by
what the user is actually working on.

ReportProvisioningStage.description:
Request body of `POST /v1/sessions/{id}/provisioning-stage`.

The daemon names the milestone; the control plane times it, exactly as it
times the stages its own provisioning queue announces. A daemon whose
clock is wrong would otherwise put its line of the timeline in 1970.

stage.description: The milestone the machine has reached.

ResizeMachine.description:
Request body of `POST /v1/sessions/{id}/machine/resize`.

The disk survives a resize; only compute is replaced. The provider and
region are not part of this, because moving a machine between them would
mean a new disk, which is a new session's problem rather than a resize.

machine_type.description: Provider-native machine type to move to, from the catalog.

text.description:
What to say to the agent. A leading `!` is the terminal escape the
UI documents; the control plane forwards the text either way and the
daemon decides.

budget.description: Budget accounting as of this request.

failure.description:
Why the session is [`SessionState::Failed`], in the provider's own
words where it has any.

`None` for every other state. A failed session that could not say
why would leave the user with a dead session and no idea whether to
retry it, pick another region, or ask for a quota increase.

SessionDetail.description: A single session, with its budget.

SessionMachine.description:
The machine a session is on, as the agent driving it is told about it.

Not the whole [`MachineCatalogEntry`]: the agent is deciding whether to
keep working here, and five facts answer that — what the machine is
called, what an hour of it costs, whether the capacity is interruptible,
how big it is, and whether starting it already committed the user to a
licence minimum. The account, the region, the family and the storage
tiers answer a different question (where flyco would provision *another*
machine) and stay in the catalog.

The same value travels three ways and means one thing in all of them: in
the bootstrap a machine boots with, in the `[machine]` table of the
daemon's configuration, and in what the agent's `machine_status` tool
reads back. Absent facts are absent from the serialized document rather
than spelled `null`, because one of those three is TOML and TOML has no
null to spell.

oneOf.description: How big it is, when the provider publishes a size.

What one hour of it costs, when flyco meters it at all.

The rate for the capacity actually held — spot when
[`spot`](Self::spot) is true and the type has a spot price. Absent on
hardware the user owns, where quoting `$0.00` would tell a budget the
session can run forever.

The floor the provider billed the moment it booted, when the type
carries one.

Present on exactly the license-bound types. An agent reading it knows
the machine has already cost [`BillingMinimum::charge`] whatever it
does next — and that moving *to* such a type is the user's decision
rather than its own.

spot.description: Whether the machine holds interruptible capacity.

oneOf.description:
Branch it works on, which the header renders as `repo · branch`
(docs/ux.md §9.1).

`None` only for a session opened before flyco recorded a branch at
all. A placeholder would be a claim about somebody's checkout that
flyco cannot support, so the header shows the repository alone for
those and every session opened since names its branch.

created_at_unix.description: When it was created, seconds since the Unix epoch.

last_active_unix.description: Last time anything happened on it, seconds since the Unix epoch.

machine_origin.description: Whether flyco or the user chose the machine it runs on.

state.description: Where it is in its lifecycle.

title.description:
What the session is called in a list.

Opens as the excerpt of the first prompt and is editable through
`PATCH /v1/sessions/{id}`. Never empty: a row with no name would
leave every list entry identified by a UUID.

SkillScope.description: Which harness's global skills directory a bundle belongs in.

SkillView.description:
One row of `GET /v1/skills`, and the response of `GET /v1/skills/{id}`.

The bundle itself is not part of this: a skill zip is object-storage
content, not a JSON field.

name.description: Directory name the bundle is installed under.

size_bytes.description: Size of the stored zip in bytes.

uploaded_at_unix.description: When it was last uploaded, seconds since the Unix epoch.

capacity_gib.description: Maximum provisioned size covered by the tier.

hourly.description: Price of the tier for one hour.

oneOf.description: A linear price for every provisioned GiB.

rate.description: Price of one GiB for one hour.

oneOf.description:
Fixed-price capacity tiers. The first tier whose capacity contains
the requested disk is the one the provider bills.

StoragePricing.description: How a provider prices the persistent disk attached to a machine.

StoredEvent.description: One stored event, as the catch-up API serves it.

at_unix.description: When the room recorded it, seconds since the Unix epoch.

seq.description:
Monotonic position in the room's stream. Pass the last one back as
`after` to continue.

TurnCursor.description: Where in a session's turn history to read from.

cursor.description:
Opaque cursor from the previous page. Omitted starts at the oldest
turn.

limit.description: How many turns to return; the control plane caps it.

TurnPage.description:
One page of `GET /v1/sessions/{id}/turns`.

The cursor is opaque: it encodes a position in the session's recorded
event stream, and a client that stores it must hand it back unread.

next_cursor.description: Cursor to pass as `cursor` for the next page, or `None` at the end.

TurnSummary.description:
One turn of a session, as the history list renders it.

Folded out of the event stream the session's room records rather than
read from a table of its own: that stream is what survives a machine and
what a browser replays, so a turn list built from anything else would
disagree with the conversation shown beside it.

completed_at_unix.description: When it finished, if it has.

prompt_excerpt.description: The opening of the user message that began the turn, for the list.

started_at_unix.description: When the turn started, seconds since the Unix epoch.

turn_id.description: Harness-native turn identifier, which is what the transcript keys on.

oneOf.description: Token accounting after the turn, when it completed.

UpdateAgentsDocument.description:
Request body of `PUT /v1/agents-md`.

Separate from [`AgentsDocument`] because
[`updated_at_unix`](AgentsDocument::updated_at_unix) is the control
plane's to stamp.

content.description: The complete new document; this replaces what is stored.

UpdateEnv.description:
Request body of `PUT /v1/sessions/{id}/env`.

Separate from [`EnvDocument`] because [`warning`](EnvDocument::warning)
is the control plane's to say: a request shape that carried it would
invite a client to submit one and be silently ignored.

entries.description: The complete new set of variables; this replaces the document.

UpdateMe.description:
Request body of `PATCH /v1/me`.

Every field is optional; an omitted field is left as it is.

UpdateMemoryNode.description:
Request body of `PATCH /v1/memory/{id}`.

An omitted field is left as it is. Reparenting is deliberately not
expressible: moving a subtree changes what every descendant is scoped to,
which is a different operation from editing a note.

title.description:
What to call the session, 1 to
[`MAX_SESSION_TITLE_CHARS`] characters once trimmed.

UploadSkill.description: What an uploaded zip is stored as.

name.description: Directory name the bundle is installed under.

scope.description:
Which harness's skills directory it belongs in. Claude Code and Codex
read different ones, so this is not derivable from the bundle.

UpsertMcpServer.description:
Request body of `POST /v1/mcp-servers` and `PATCH /v1/mcp-servers/{id}`.

A patch carries the whole document rather than a diff: an MCP server's
configuration is small, and a half-applied transport change is a state
nobody should be able to describe.

enabled.description: Whether sessions are given this server at all.

name.description: Name the harness announces the server under. Unique per user.

UsageReport.description: Token and context-window accounting reported by the harness.

oneOf.description:
Context-window fill, when the harness reports both halves of it.

Codex reports `modelContextWindow` on every token-usage
notification; the Claude Agent SDK only names a window size when its
`result` message carries per-model usage, so this is `None` for
sessions where it does not.
Cost estimate reported by the harness for this session, if any.

input_tokens.description: Input tokens consumed so far in this session.

output_tokens.description: Output tokens produced so far in this session.

VapidPublicKey.description:
Response of `GET /v1/push/vapid-public-key`.

The SPA passes this to `PushManager.subscribe` as
`applicationServerKey`; the matching private key never leaves the
control plane.

key.description: The uncompressed P-256 public point, base64url without padding.
